tasks.name: code-context-and-delimiters

tasks.name: common-markdown-and-mapping
tasks.evidence: List hanging indent, physical/task/tab continuations and quote depth/continuity pass on both Linux engines. Table separator scanning shares escape/code context. Inline tokenizer covers escapes, variable-width code, underscore/nested emphasis, strikethrough and inline links. All current projected text and DOM boundaries use explicit row-relative source intervals; native Select All includes hidden prefixes. Full Linux suite and classic regressions passed with explicit Xvfb rendering fallback. Setext titles and closed initial front matter now pass native Linux opening/edit/undo/mode probes. Reference links, images, nested/container code, cross-row inline projection and remaining block/unsupported-literal contexts still pending. URI/email angle autolinks and plain URL/email recognition now use explicit raw intervals. Unsafe schemes have no executable browser href; code and escaped angles remain literal. Directed Linux DOM-caret/undo/CRLF/mode checks and codec checks on all three platforms pass. The full Linux run passed all checks except B1, whose multi-node targeting was fixed and passed separately; eleven classic checks are green. Native external activation and remaining Markdown contexts are not complete. Inline link grammar now separates decoded destination and title, handles escaped/balanced parentheses and angle paths with spaces, and decodes standard character references once without reinterpreting escaped entities. Nested explicit links and angle autolinks take precedence without nested anchors. Styled labels (including UTF16 emoji prefixes) and empty labels pass native Linux editing/undo/CRLF/mode probes. The full Linux suite is green and codec probes pass on all three platforms. Reference definitions and cross-row inline projection remain pending. Reference-link development now passes native Linux browser probes for Unicode/full/collapsed/shortcut resolution, first-definition precedence, editable multiline definitions, dependent prose/table refresh, unrelated DOM preservation, undo and CRLF/mode round-trip. Codec checks pass on Linux/macOS/Windows; eleven classic checks pass. Cross-row inline projection and nested-container completeness remain pending. The dedicated blocking REQ-I3 contract gate now passes both Linux engines; projections and the operational risk register are synchronized.

tasks.name: enter-tab-and-local-cleanup
tasks.evidence: Tab/Shift+Tab in both modes preserves mixed terminators, list subtrees and oriented selections, with undo/redo. Visual prose Enter now generates one local hard-break marker, hides its syntax, removes owned markers for paragraph creation/Backspace joins and protects literal escaping or explicitly retyped source. Provenance survives row indentation. Full Linux suite and eleven isolated regression scripts passed. Structure-transition cleanup, remaining boundary operations, general gesture planning and actual recovery persistence are still pending. Forward Delete now joins owned boundaries atomically with undo/provenance restoration, including mixed terminators and literal escaping; full Linux suite and eleven regressions passed. Structural transitions after an owned boundary now remove the redundant marker in the same transaction, with manual-marker preservation and undo restoration. Cleanup within larger transformed units and recovery integration remain pending.

tasks.name: clipboard
tasks.evidence: Safe PRE conversion already implemented. Clipboard core now supports visual/source copy/cut/paste, validated internal payload, plain Markdown/semantic HTML, partial inline delimiters, transactional cut and exact source-mode edits. Directed controlled-clipboard tests pass both Linux engines and all thirteen classic checks pass. Structured fragments, external conversion completeness and real native/system clipboard acceptance remain pending. HTML lists retain nesting and ordered numbering, headings and recursive quotes retain markers, and tables acquire header/separator and escaped pipes. Directed helper tests, REQ-D1 on both Linux engines and all thirteen classic regressions pass. Conversion edge cases and actual system clipboard remain pending. Copied references now include required definitions. Internal visual paste scopes incoming labels, preserving existing destinations and undo; table-cell reference dependencies and REQ-I3 pass both Linux engines. Semantic HTML fallback for copied reference links and real clipboard acceptance remain pending.

tasks.name: settings-and-active-line
tasks.evidence: Backend validated settings store and load/save commands implemented. Two directed store tests and all 27 Linux Rust tests pass. UI, font factors, visual-line overlay, focus reload and package acceptance remain pending. Settings dialog, isolated preview, defaults, Save/Cancel/retry and focus reload are implemented. Directed browser tests pass both Linux engines; font factors preserve source and selection and recompute table padding. Active visual-line overlay and native package acceptance are still pending. Current-line overlay and effective settings in Bug snapshots are implemented. Soft-wrap, backward active endpoint, source geometry, focus visibility and code viewport clipping pass both Linux engines; all twelve classic regressions pass. Container-boundary selection, isolated highlight preview and native acceptance remain pending. Container-boundary Select All in both directions, isolated palette preview and destroyed-preview viewport cleanup now pass both Linux engines. A single final twelve-test regression run passes after explicit final-input synchronization in prose/list probes. Dedicated Settings contract and native acceptance remain pending. REQ-J1 is now a blocking QA gate. The full current Linux suite passes all 37 automated requirements (38 declared including one manual advisory). Updated full Rust tests also pass on macOS (28) and Windows (26), with identical source archive hashes verified. Native preference IPC/restart/concurrent-window/package acceptance remains pending.

tasks.name: file-actions-recovery-and-windows
tasks.evidence: Separate leased recovery records for concurrent same-path sessions and untitled documents; explicit same-document selection, own-copy discard/save, exact legacy import receipts and retained originals. Native Linux crash/restart, choice/cancel, early Save and migration probes, final full Linux suite, eleven editor regressions and thirteen Rust checks on all three platforms passed. File actions, cross-document recovery UI and changed-base recovery remain pending. Shared canonical-path locks now protect saves, including occupied temporary slots, absent/deleted destinations and other-instance conflicts. Blocking I/O is off the UI thread; a captured save leaves newer edits dirty, with recovery persisted during lock wait and rebased after commit. Obsolete document context commands are rejected. New/Open now stage file validation and recovery choices before replacing context, with Save/Discard/Cancel, fresh untitled sessions and history reset on successful Open. Rust checks on all platforms and the full 31-requirement Linux suite pass, including actual menu visibility, shortcuts, recovery-choice cancellation and unrelated-copy preservation. Save As preserves context and history on cancellation/failure, validates the destination snapshot and changes identity only after a successful write. Empty and edited untitled Save, Save before New and subsequent Save to the new path pass native Linux probes. The full 32-requirement Linux suite is green; Rust checks pass on Linux, Windows and macOS. Independent windows, Finder events and cross-document/changed-base recovery remain pending. New window and Open in new window now launch separate processes without replacing the original editor, with native Linux process-lifetime, cancellation, argument and debug probes passing. Launch-plan checks pass on all three platforms. Finder lifecycle and package-level rendered child acceptance remain pending. Finder lifecycle now queues RunEvent::Opened requests until frontend readiness, deduplicates canonical startup aliases and routes the first unused window separately from later independent instances. Invalid/missing targets report errors without creating files; requests wait for ongoing dialogs/actions. Five routing probes, queue tests and complete Rust suites pass on all three platforms. The 34-requirement Linux suite passed before the final fresh-untitled flag; all native Linux workflows passed after it. Actual Finder/Dock package acceptance remains pending.
